transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-15
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Sophie (Redwood AE), Ravi (CSM), Lena (SE), Dr. Amanda Reyes, Marcus Lin, Tara Brooks, Samir Patel

[00:00] Sophie: hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Sophie from Redwood, i'm the account lead, we also have ravi and lena from our success and se teams. how's everyone doing?
[00:12] Amanda: good, thanks. small delay here but looks good.
[00:18] Marcus: morning from my side.
[00:22] Sophie: great - quick agenda, we'll run through onboarding milestones, access and SSO, deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), security/compliance questions, and then define pilot scope and next steps. any additions?
[00:34] Samir: maybe also discuss model choices for the pilot and latency expectations.
[00:38] Sophie: yes good call we'll put that in.

[02:05] Lena: hi team, quick intro from me - i'll be leading the technical onboarding, benchmarks and the pilot runs. for context, Mayfield what are the primary user flows? maybe samir you can share?
[02:18] Samir: sure - primary flows are clinical note summarization, automated triage suggestions, and patient messaging templates. volume initially small - maybe a few hundred requests per day but peak times for triage may spike. latency target is sub-1s for single-turn prompt is ideal but we understand tradeoffs.
[02:40] Lena: great, that helps. for the pilot we usually recommend a hosted pilot to get baseline metrics, then we can scope dedicated capacity or private VPC if you need data isolation.

[04:00] Tara: from security/compliance, we need to confirm where data is stored, audit logs, encryption at rest and in transit, and whether we can bring our KMS. We do have SSO via Okta and we need SCIM provisioning for user access. SOC2 report would be required for procurement.
[04:28] Ravi: we can share Redwood's SOC2 Type II and our compliance package. we also support SSO via SAML and SCIM for provisioning. KMS integration is available for private deployments; for hosted we offer customer-managed keys in some regions, we can follow up with specifics.
[04:45] Tara: perfect, can you send the details? also any support for attribute-based access or RBAC?
[04:52] Sophie: yes RBAC is supported; we'll include a roles matrix in the checklist.

[06:10] Marcus: about private deployment - what's the typical lead time and what's required from our infra side?
[06:20] Lena: private deployments (VPC connector or on-prem) usually take 4-6 weeks to provision depending on network approvals. we'll need subnet details, NAT/egress rules, and firewall rules for our proxy. for the pilot we recommend starting hosted so we can run benchmarks in 1-2 weeks, then if results look good move to a dedicated pool or a private connector.
[06:48] Marcus: ok that aligns with our timelines. one of our constraints is strict egress rules, can you support egress-restricted setups?
[06:56] Lena: yes for private connectors we can go through bastion/proxy patterns and we can support limited egress, you'll need to open a few endpoints for control plane and telemetry. we'll provide a whitelist.

[09:10] Samir: on cost, do you have a recommended config for clinical workloads - quantized models or lower precision? we want to balance quality vs cost.
[09:22] Sophie: good question - our Optimize team recommends starting with a 4-bit quantized LLM variant for many production tasks; for sensitive clinical summarization we often run a mixed approach: high-precision model for final scoring or critical flows and a cheaper quantized path for drafts. we'll include model recommendation notes in the pilot doc.
[09:48] Lena: also we'll run throughput vs latency benchmarks across sequence lengths you provide and propose batching configs.

[11:00] Tara: another compliance question - retention policy, can we set auto-delete or restrict retention for logs and model cache?
[11:10] Ravi: yes, retention policies are configurable. for private deployments retention can be set to your policy and we can disable long-term storage. audit logs are exportable for your SIEM.

[12:40] Amanda: what's the typical SLO for hosted API? we need a baseline for SLA discussions.
[12:48] Sophie: for hosted we publish latency percentiles per model in the catalog, and for dedicated we offer SLA-backed targets depending on commit. we'll share our published p50/p95 tables, but we can also set custom SLOs if you go dedicated or private with reserved capacity.

[15:05] Marcus: do you have any customers in healthcare with similar compliance needs? helps procurement feel comfortable.
[15:14] Ravi: yes we have several healthcare customers on private deployments; i'll include two references and an anonymized architecture doc. note: some names may be slightly off in the transcript, apologies if i mis-say - that's the auto-transcript voice.

[17:00] Lena: ok for the pilot technical plan i propose: week 0 (this week) - access and accounts, week 1-2 - baseline hosted benchmark with your sample payloads, week 3 - analyze results and tune batching/quantization, week 4 - pilot review and decision to move to dedicated or private. does that timeline work?
[17:25] Marcus: that looks doable. we have a regulatory review on 2027-03-30, so ideally the pilot review happens before that.
[17:35] Samir: yes can we target final review week of 4/5 so procurement can start?
[17:41] Sophie: we can schedule the pilot kickoff for 2027-04-05 and aim to have the review meeting week of 2027-04-26 if needed.

[20:00] Tara: about SSO and SCIM, our Okta team needs a template for SAML metadata and SCIM groups. can you provide the endpoints and sample manifest?
[20:12] Lena: yes we'll provide a SCIM manifest and SAML metadata. we'll also include role mappings for RBAC.

[22:15] Amanda: model selection - are there Redwood-verified models for clinical summarization or do you mostly host open models?
[22:25] Sophie: Redwood curates a catalog of open models and publishes verified performance profiles. for clinical summarization we typically test a few LLMs and pick the best quality/latency tradeoff. we can also onboard customer-provided models if you have internally tuned ones.
[22:48] Lena: note: transcription may say 'Redwood optimize' or other things incorrectly - we'll send a clean doc with the model names and versions.

[25:05] Samir: on evals, can you tie quality regressions to prompt sets or production prompts? we'd like to have automatic regression alerts.
[25:20] Ravi: yes our Console supports quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to eval prompt sets. we'll set up an initial evaluation harness for the pilot.

[27:40] Marcus: any special networking requirements for the hosted pilot? we have strict firewall rules.
[27:50] Lena: hosted pilot only requires outbound to our public control plane endpoints; we'll give you a minimal whitelist of domains and IP ranges. if the firewall is too strict we can instead run a private connector in a pre-prod VPC.

[30:00] Tara: procurement will ask about indemnity and data usage: do you train models on customer data?
[30:10] Sophie: we do not train customer data into our public model catalogue; for hosted we have options to opt-out of data retention for model training and for private deployments no customer data is used to train our public models. we'll include the exact language in our data processing addendum.

[32:00] Lena: quick technical note: for throughput tests we'll need a representative distribution of prompt lengths and expected concurrency. if you can share a small sample of anonymized prompts that will help.
[32:15] Amanda: we'll prepare a sanitized set by 2027-03-19.

[34:30] Sophie: ok team, to recap action items - Sophie to send pricing and onboarding checklist, ravi to share SOC2 and references, lena to prepare benchmark scripts and SAML/SCIM manifests, tara to circulate compliance questions. any changes?
[34:48] Tara: that's right. also please include KMS integration detail for private deployment.
[34:55] Lena: we'll include KMS docs and sample key rotation notes.

[37:00] Samir: one last question on metrics - how do you track cost per inference and what dashboards will we see?
[37:10] Ravi: Console provides token-level cost breakdown, per-route/model dashboards, and tracing hooks. we'll give you view-only access to a sample account so you can see cost dashboards.

[40:00] Marcus: do you have recommended guardrails for PHI-in-scope prompts? we'd like to avoid sending identifiable data to hosted environments.
[40:12] Sophie: yes we recommend PII/PHI redaction at the app layer prior to calls for hosted; for private deployments we can keep everything within your VPC and use customer-managed keys. we'll include a PHI handling checklist.

[44:00] Lena: scheduling note - i'll book a technical pre-kickoff with Marcus and his infra person next week to go over subnet and egress requirements.
[44:12] Marcus: thanks, i'll invite James from infra.

[47:30] Amanda: procurement will want to see an estimated run-rate for the pilot - can you give a ballpark?
[47:40] Sophie: we'll include a conservative estimate in the pricing worksheet, usually pilots are low-cost and we can structure a time-limited credit if needed.

[50:05] Sophie: ok final recap and confirm next steps: send onboarding checklist and pricing by 3/17, customer provides SSO and sample prompts by 3/19, SE runs hosted benchmark and shares results by 3/22, schedule pilot kickoff 4/05.
[50:25] Amanda: confirmed. thanks everyone.
[50:32] Samir: thanks.
[50:36] Ravi: thanks all, i'll share the compliance pack after the call.
[50:40] Lena: bye everyone.
[50:45] End of recording.
notes: Transcript contains typical ASR imperfections; speaker labels approximate. References to docs: onboarding checklist link (shared post-call), SOC2 package (link), example benchmark scripts (link).
